description: Behaviour every language binding must implement identically: which native error codes are worth retrying, the reconnect backoff schedule, how a reconnect checkpoint replaces the configured start position, what happens when the optional metadata connection fails, and the shared option defaults with their accepted ranges. Each binding keeps a mirror of this table (Node: src/contract.ts, Python: _contract.py) and a contract test that compares the mirror against this file, so changing a constant on one surface alone fails that surface's test suite.

checkpointResume.rule: A non-empty checkpoint becomes the successor connection's start GTID and clears any file/offset anchor. An empty checkpoint means none was ever published, so the configured start mode is kept verbatim: forwarding an empty GTID set would ask the server for every binlog it still retains.
checkpointResume.clearedValue: Each binding reports a cleared or unset start-position field as null in the normalized form used by the contract tests.

cases.name: empty checkpoint keeps a file/offset anchor
empty checkpoint keeps the current-position start mode
empty checkpoint keeps an explicitly configured start GTID
published checkpoint replaces a file/offset anchor
published checkpoint replaces an explicitly configured start GTID

checkpointRetention.rule: The stream's checkpoint accessor keeps returning the last non-empty checkpoint after the native client is released, so the documented pattern of persisting it after leaving the iteration scope works on every surface.
checkpointRetention.readRule: The native checkpoint advances as events leave the client queue, so one read covers a whole poll batch. Reading it per decoded row event is a defect: the cost then scales with row count instead of batch count.

metadataError.rule: When the optional column-name metadata connection cannot be enabled and no metadata-error handler is configured, the binding stays silent: no warning, no stderr write. The library never writes diagnostics on its own; embedders opt in through the handler or through the native log callback.

iteration.rule: Leaving an iteration early does not release native resources on its own. Every binding exposes an async close on the stream (Node: Symbol.asyncDispose / close(), Python: aclose() / close()) and documents the scoped form (`await using` / `async with`) as the supported usage.

logLevel.rule: Installing a log handler with a level outside the documented mes_log_level_t range is an error, never a silently disabled callback.

requiredTogether.rule: Both options of a pair are supplied together or neither is, and the whole-config entry point that received them rejects a configuration supplying one alone: an offset without the file it points into names no position a server can start from, so a binding that accepted it would discard the offset and replicate from somewhere the caller never asked for. The refusal belongs to the entry points that see a whole configuration, because a per-key validator cannot see the companion. This is a different statement from the conditional floor an option entry may carry: the floor says what a supplied value must be once its companion is set, this says whether the option may appear alone at all.
requiredTogether.unsetRule: Whether an option counts as supplied is decided by the surface's own spelling of an absent option. A surface that can spell absence spells it that way and states nothing here (Node leaves the key out or sets it to undefined). A surface whose signature declares a plain integer cannot, so it states the value it passes when nothing was requested, and that value counts as unset: it is below the option's conditional floor and therefore never a position the option could have been asked to start from. The consequence is stated rather than hidden: a Python caller who passes that value explicitly is indistinguishable from one who passed nothing, so it is accepted there and refused on Node.

optionsRule: Every entry states the accepted range each binding must enforce for the option. An entry that also carries `default` states the value the binding materializes when the option is omitted; an entry without `default` (a start-position selector) has no default to agree on and is range-checked only. A selector may also state a tighter floor that holds only while the companion option it names is set: the stated range stays in force when that companion is unset, because the value a binding passes through then is the one that means no start position was requested. Naming a companion states when the floor applies and nothing more: whether the two options may appear alone is the sibling requiredTogether rule, not this one. The first binlog event begins after the file's 4-byte magic number, which is why an offset into a named file cannot be below 4.
